# Signing-key id (`kid`) vectors — provenance

**`signing-key-ids.json` was not generated by this SDK, and must never be
regenerated from it.**

The `kid` an offline `.lic`/`.mach` file names is
`lowercase_hex(SHA-256(<the public key STRING>)[0..8])` — 16 hex characters —
per the server's own `key_id()` in `tamga-api/src/shared/crypto/license_file.rs`.
These vectors were produced by an independent SHA-256 implementation and then
confirmed against `tamga-rust`'s committed vector `51643eac9777b63a`.

## Why this matters

This repo has already shipped the failure mode this rule exists to prevent.
`test/helpers/checkoutFixtures.ts` made the same ECDSA mistake on the *signing*
side that `src/crypto/ecdsa.ts` made on the *verifying* side, so the round trip
was green while no server-issued ECDSA machine file could be verified. A fixture
an SDK produced can only ever prove that the SDK agrees with itself.

**Do not add a vector computed by this repository to this file.** If a case is
missing, have it produced by an implementation that is not this one.

## The trap these vectors pin

The server hands `key_id()` the **stored base64 string**, never the 32 decoded
key bytes. The natural assumption — that a key id hashes the key — is wrong, and
an implementation that decodes first produces a plausible-looking id that
matches nothing the server ever emits, which reports every authentic file as
signed by an unknown key.

`negative` in the JSON pins both halves for one key: `correctKid`
(`905f28def18eaac0`) and `wrongKidIfDecodedFirst` (`630dcd2966c43366`).
`test/signing-key-id.spec.ts` asserts **both** — that the implementation
produces the first and does not produce the second. The positive assertion alone
does not catch the trap, because a decode-first implementation simply fails it
without ever naming what went wrong.

## Contents

| vector | what it catches |
| --- | --- |
| `all_zero_key` | the primary vector; shared with `tamga-rust` |
| `unbackfilled_account` | `key_id("")` = `e3b0c44298fc1c14` — the id every file gets from an account whose `ed25519_public_key` column was never populated |
| `sequential_bytes` | a digest that is reversed or reordered |
| `high_bytes` | a byte `>= 0x80` sign-extended into hex |
| `leading_zero_digest` | a hex byte that is not zero-padded to two characters |
| `negative` | hashing the decoded bytes instead of the base64 string |

## One edit was made to the source file

The generator that produced the upstream copy interpolated the output of `id(1)`
into a single prose sentence in `_provenance.servedAs`, which read
`...as the resource uid=501(...) gid=20(...) groups=...;`. That sentence is
repaired here to its evident intent (`...as the resource id;`). **No vector was
touched**: every `publicKey`, `kid`, `correctKid` and `wrongKidIfDecodedFirst`
value in this file is byte-identical to the upstream copy, and each one is
independently re-derived at test time rather than trusted.
